items.note: In all forts there should be a rampart and moat and exit-gates; the rampart 12 cubits high, of bricks.
A town is called a capital only with gopura gates in four directions, guard-houses, army-quarters, merchants, markets and many temples.
Besides the Samarangana-sutradhara, Bhoj's Yukti-kalpataru also treats town-founding briefly; a town should be founded at an auspicious time.
Aparajita-priccha, by Bhuvanadeva of the 12th-13th century, also treats this subject; chapter 70 names town kinds Bhudhara, Hemakuta and Ratnakuta.
Prescribed swings at the spring festival, covered dance-halls facing the deity, a sacrifice-pavilion and a monastery with ascetics' meditation-hall.
Deities should be neither north-facing nor south-facing; those outside the rampart face the town.
Prescribed quarters for craftsmen, washermen, cloth-printers, leather-workers, liquor-sellers and weavers, with spinning-wheels in the town.
Six kinds of tank, embankment dimensions, and building of many stepwells, wells and tanks with festivals.
Ten wells, four stepwells, four kundas and six kinds of tank prescribed for inside and outside the town.
Four kinds of stepwell (Nanda, Bhadra, Jaya, Vijaya) distinguished by number of mouths and terraces.
Bhoj built a vast dam on the Betwa; the lake had an area of about 250 square miles and gave irrigation; Hoshang Shah of Mandu later broke it.
Besides the Bhojpur lake Bhoj built several other tanks, still visible at Dhar, Ujjain and Mandav.
Bhoj's Charu-charya survives in several forms, the largest at Mysore, with a Jala-mangala section on the properties of waters.
